text: Methods for evaluating toxic substances that cause hearing impairment in experimental animals are described. In the experiments reported here, animals were trained using positive reinforcement operant conditioning procedures to examine their hearing behaviorally. When normal hearing was achieved, aminoglycoside antibiotics (kanamycin and dihydrostreptomycin) were administered daily, and hearing tests were conducted to monitor the progression of hearing loss over time. Initially, there was an increase in sensitivity to high-frequency sounds, but this eventually led to a decline in sensitivity to low-frequency sounds. These changes in hearing corresponded with a decrease in receptor cells within the inner ear, starting from the base of the cochlea and moving towards the apex. While such behavioral procedures may require moderate instrumentation costs and take some time to implement, they have been shown to provide accurate quantitative measurements of hearing. Additionally, these methods allow for the early detection of the toxic process and the precise correlation between behavioral impairment and concurrent histopathological changes occurring simultaneously in the inner ear and auditory nerve.
